Large-n shapes (n=1024/2048/4096) are compute-bound on the O(n^3) trailing-matrix updates. Write a right-looking BLOCKED Householder QR whose trailing GEMMs (V^T A and (I - V T V^T) A) run on Blackwell tensor cores in TF32 (try BF16) with FP32 accumulate, while the panel factorization, the reflector vectors V, and tau stay STRICTLY FP32 to preserve the orthogonality (rtol 100*n*eps) and factor-residual tolerances. Maximize arithmetic intensity with fewer, larger tensor-core launches. Reduced precision must touch only the trailing apply GEMMs, never the reflectors.

Blocked Householder QR, TF32 tensor-core trailing GEMMs, FP32 panel+V+tau. n=1024 shapes 6.1x faster (escapes serial cusolver batch loop); n=2048/4096 regress (panel under-parallelized for small batch). Validate+3 guards CLEAN. Geomean 86976 us (1.29x vs 112384 baseline).

nb=16 for n=1024: shapes 20.6k->18.2k us (11.8x). Validate+3 guards CLEAN. Geomean 60494 us (1.857x).

Route n=4096 to geqrf (removes 0.95x regression); fold T into Y=V*T^T removing middle trailing GEMM. Validate+3 guards CLEAN. Geomean 60375 us (1.861x). Split for n=1024: panel 33%, V/S/T 16%, trailing 51% (bandwidth-bound).
Custom batched panel+nb=16 for n=2048 (beats cuSOLVER even at batch=8): 65k->28.8k us (2.41x). n=1024 18.2k (11.8x), n=4096->geqrf. Validate+3 guards CLEAN. Geomean 56235 us (1.999x ~2x).
Warp-shuffle block reduction in panel kernel (1 sync/reduce vs log(nt)). n=1024 18.2k->16.6k (13.0x), n=2048 28.8k->24.4k (2.85x). Validate+3 guards CLEAN. Geomean 54321 us (2.069x).

Two-level blocked QR: outer NB=64 super-panel applies to full trailing once per 64 cols (few large GEMMs), inner nb=16 panels confined to the block. n=1024 16.6k->12.0k (18.0x), n=2048 24.0k (2.89x). Validate+3 guards CLEAN. Geomean ~49900 us (2.25x).
Tune outer NB=128 (swept: best for both shapes). n=1024 ~11.36k (19.0x), n=2048 ~23.68k (2.93x). Validate+3 guards CLEAN. Geomean ~49200 us (2.286x).

Fast tiled batched transpose in-extension (replace torch .transpose().contiguous()). blocked_qr takes row-major A, returns {H,tau}. n=1024 ~11.18k, n=2048 ~23.54k. Validate+3 guards CLEAN. Geomean ~48970 us (2.294x).

Final: header docs + nsys profile of n=2048. Profile shows panel_factor 56% (8-CTA occupancy-bound), build_T 11% (b=128 outer recurrence), trailing tensor-core GEMMs the rest. Geomean ~48985 us (2.294x). n=1024 ~19x, n=2048 ~2.94x, n=4096->geqrf.

Best: 49006 us geomean = 2.293x vs baseline 112384 (commit ba57274f). Built a two-level right-looking blocked Householder QR (custom CUDA geqr2 panel kernel + cuBLAS strided-batched trailing GEMMs + cuSOLVER fallback), dispatched by SIZE n only. Wins: n=1024 (3 shapes) ~19x, n=2048 ~2.9x; n=4096 routed to torch.geqrf (no regression). What worked: (1) the DOMINANT win is BATCHING the trailing GEMMs to escape torch.geqrf's serial per-matrix cusolver loop (n>256 -> looped cusolverDnSgeqrf); a custom batched FP32 panel (one CTA/matrix, warp-shuffle reductions) + nb=16 + batched trailing GEMMs gives 19x on n=1024 b60 and 2.9x on n=2048 b8 even at low occupancy; (2) two-level blocking (inner nb=16 panel, outer NB=128 super-panel applied to the full trailing) decouples cheap panel from low-traffic trailing -> +~1.4x on n=1024; (3) custom tiled transpose beat torch's. KEY FINDING contradicting the brief premise: the blocked trailing update is BANDWIDTH-bound (rank-nb rewrite of trailing, AI~nb/4), so TF32 tensor cores give NO speedup at small NB and only ~10-15% once NB=128 raises arithmetic intensity. FP32 and TF32 hold the residual/orthogonality gates with wide margin (TF32 kept). What didn't: more threads/CTA for the panel (occupancy-bound, not throughput-bound); shared-memory panel (load/store > reuse at nb=16); recursive block larft for build_T (too many tiny launches, regressed). REMAINING BOTTLENECK: the FP32 panel factorization dominates n=2048 (~56-68% of time, profiled) because only 8 matrices -> 8 CTAs -> 8/188 SMs. SUGGESTIONS for next briefs: (a) a multi-CTA / cooperative-groups or TSQR panel to use the idle SMs for small-batch large-n (n=2048, maybe revisit n=4096) -- but a cooperative grid-sync costs ~1us and the panel needs ~2n syncs, so it is marginal unless sync count is cut; (b) n=4096 (batch=2) still on geqrf -- a single-matrix (non-batched) tensor-core QR path could try to beat cuSOLVER there; (c) the small-n (n=32/176/352) and n=512 b640 shapes are untouched here (other workers' territory) and dominate the absolute geomean. Also hit (and mostly fixed) a cross-CTA race where non-row-0 CTAs read x[0] as alpha while CTA-0 overwrote it with beta -- fixed by capturing alpha to global before the v-formation; a residual orthogonality error remained, but the PERFORMANCE verdict (2x slower) was already decisive and independent of correctness.
